title: crdt-note-blob — case shape (v0.2)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::encode_crdt_note_blob_raw + protocol::decode_crdt_note_blob — the NC05 per-note CRDT blob, the first next-major format to be allocated (automerge-sync-migration, myne-md/myne#418; docs/spec/protocol.md §10.7). An NC05 blob is the §9.2 envelope with exactly three substitutions and nothing else: magic NC05 (not MY01), header protocol_version byte 0x02 (not 0x01), and both AEAD tags binding the v0.2 AAD prefix 'myne.v0.2|' (not 'myne.v0.1|') via aad_nc05_item_key_wrap / aad_nc05_content_encrypt. No new SubkeyRole is introduced — the key lineage is the v0.1 one. The inner plaintext is OPAQUE: it is the note's Automerge save() output and the codec never parses it, exactly as MY01 never parses markdown. Five case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per §6.4 — including the load-bearing v0.1-AAD domain-separation case), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject), 'aad_construction' (canonical AAD bytes for the two NC05 builders). Reference implementation: protocol/src/crdt_note_blob.rs (main myne repository).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'crdt-note-blob/v0.2/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_items_key_hex.description: 32-byte singleton itemsKey (hex) — the KEK the per-note item_key is wrapped under.

input_items_key_id_hex.description: 16-byte items_key_id (hex). AAD-bound by both NC05 builders and carried verbatim in the header, so a blob written under a rotated itemsKey is distinguishable before any decryption is attempted.

input_note_uuid_hex.description: 16-byte note UUID (hex). AAD-bound but NOT stored in the blob — the caller supplies it from the filename, which is what stops a blob being relocated onto another note's identity.

input_item_key_hex.description: 32-byte per-note item_key (hex), caller-supplied for determinism (the _raw suffix convention). Production callers source it from a CSPRNG.

input_item_key_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex) for the item_key wrap.

input_content_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex) for the content encryption. MUST differ from the item_key nonce: the two AEAD operations use different keys, but reusing one nonce value across a blob is the habit that eventually reuses it under one key.

input_plaintext_hex.description: Opaque inner plaintext (hex) — the note's Automerge save() bytes. The codec never parses these; a port must treat them as an uninterpreted byte string, exactly as MY01 treats markdown.

expected_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (header + wrapped item_key + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex-encoded lowercase. Decoders compare byte-equal. The first four bytes are 4e433035 ('NC05') and the fifth is 02.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: Recovered opaque Automerge bytes (hex). Byte-equal to the encrypt case's input_plaintext_hex.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a single non-distinguishing failure (Rust reference: CannotDecryptCrdtNote). Wrong itemsKey, tampered ciphertext, a relocated note_uuid and a v0.1-AAD blob must all collapse to the same outcome (§6.4). The v0.1-AAD case is the load-bearing member: a structurally perfect NC05 blob whose tags were computed under 'myne.v0.1|' must fail to open, which is the whole reason the prefix is a major-version-event constant rather than cosmetics.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. Rejected BEFORE any decryption: magic, protocol_version, reserved-byte and length checks all run first (§10.1 strict-trailing included). These fixtures carry the REAL keys on purpose — the header is not AAD-bound, so a port that skips a structural check decodes Ok and the runner catches it; dummy keys would mask the bug as a coincidental AEAD failure.

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST reject structurally rather than reporting an AEAD failure. The two version-boundary members are the §10.5 anti-downgrade pins: an MY01 magic must not parse as NC05, and an NC05 blob carrying protocol_version 0x01 must not parse either.

oneOf.title: aad_construction — pin an NC05 AAD builder's canonical bytes

input_aad_builder.description: Which NC05 AAD builder the case pins. These two are the note-scoped half of the v0.2 AAD family; the four vault-scoped v0.2 builders live in the aad-construction/v0.2 category instead, one home per builder.

expected_aad_hex.description: Canonical AAD bytes (hex). Opens with 6d796e652e76302e327c ('myne.v0.2|') followed by the 0x02 version byte — the two bytes-level facts that domain-separate every v0.2 tag from its v0.1 counterpart.
